{"subject": "Flow Step Output", "description": "Consolidated final TypeScript implementation spec for the Exaix request/plan API, reconciling two redundant prior passes", "steps": [{"step": 1, "title": "Duplication note", "description": "Step 1 and Step 2 of this task's input are two independent implementations of the same design (same types, same handlers, same SSE resume logic) rather than sequential build-on-each-other work — likely a flow replay or re-run rather than intentional iteration. Since neither adds new scope, this step reconciles them into a single canonical spec instead of producing a third variant, picking the stronger naming/structure choice at each point of divergence and noting why."}, {"step": 2, "title": "Core domain types (canonical)", "description": "```typescript
type RequestStatus =
  | "queued"
  | "planning"
  | "running"
  | "cancelling"
  | "succeeded"
  | "failed"
  | "cancelled";

const TERMINAL_STATUSES: ReadonlySet<RequestStatus> = new Set([
  "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled",
]);

const VALID_TRANSITIONS: Readonly<Record<RequestStatus, readonly RequestStatus[]>> = {
  queued: ["planning", "cancelled"],
  planning: ["running", "failed"],
  running: ["succeeded", "failed", "cancelling"],
  cancelling: ["cancelled", "succeeded"],
  succeeded: [],
  failed: [],
  cancelled: [],
};

function isValidTransition(from: RequestStatus, to: RequestStatus): boolean {
  return VALID_TRANSITIONS[from].includes(to);
}

interface RequestProgress {
  percent: number;
  currentStep: string | null;
  totalSteps: number;
}

interface ExaixRequest {
  id: string;
  tenantId: string;
  status: RequestStatus;
  input: Record<string, unknown>;
  result: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  error: { code: string; message: string } | null;
  planId: string | null;
  progress: RequestProgress | null;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
}

type PlanStepStatus = "pending" | "running" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "skipped";

interface PlanStep {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  status: PlanStepStatus;
  startedAt: string | null;
  finishedAt: string | null;
}

interface Plan {
  id: string;
  version: number;
  requestId: string;
  steps: PlanStep[];
  createdAt: string;
}
```
Kept step 1's explicit `VALID_TRANSITIONS` table (step 2 dropped it) alongside step 2's `ReadonlySet` typing for `TERMINAL_STATUSES` (tighter than step 1's `Set<RequestStatus>`) — both the enumerable transition table and the O(1) terminal check are needed by the handlers below, and neither variant alone had both."}, {"step": 3, "title": "Error hierarchy (canonical)", "description": "```typescript
interface ErrorBody {
  error: { code: string; message: string; retryable: boolean };
}

abstract class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly code: string,
    message: string,
    public readonly statusCode: number,
    public readonly retryable: boolean,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = this.constructor.name;
  }
  toBody(): ErrorBody {
    return { error: { code: this.code, message: this.message, retryable: this.retryable } };
  }
}

class ValidationError extends ApiError {
  constructor(message: string, public readonly field?: string) {
    super("VALIDATION_ERROR", message, 400, false);
  }
}
class UnauthenticatedError extends ApiError {
  constructor() { super("UNAUTHENTICATED", "Authentication required", 401, false); }
}
class NotFoundError extends ApiError {
  constructor() { super("NOT_FOUND", "Resource not found", 404, false); }
}
class ConflictError extends ApiError {
  constructor(message: string) { super("CONFLICT", message, 409, false); }
}
class RateLimitedError extends ApiError {
  constructor(public readonly retryAfterSeconds: number) {
    super("RATE_LIMITED", "Too many requests", 429, true);
  }
}
class InternalError extends ApiError {
  constructor() { super("INTERNAL_ERROR", "Internal server error", 500, true); }
}
```
Used step 2's flat constructor style (`code, message, statusCode, retryable` all passed to `super()`) instead of step 1's abstract-getter style, since it needs one fewer line per subclass and avoids the TS requirement to redeclare `abstract readonly statusCode`/`retryable` on every subclass. `NotFoundError`'s message stays fixed and generic in both variants — required so cross-tenant access and missing-ID both return an identical body, per the architect's A01 note."}, {"step": 4, "title": "Atomic status transitions (canonical, named casTransition)", "description": "```typescript
interface StatusStore {
  casTransition(
    requestId: string,
    tenantId: string,
    from: readonly RequestStatus[],
    to: RequestStatus,
  ): Promise<boolean>; // true iff this call performed the write
}

async function cancelRequest(
  store: StatusStore,
  requestId: string,
  tenantId: string,
  current: ExaixRequest,
): Promise<{ status: RequestStatus }> {
  if (TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(current.status)) {
    throw new ConflictError(`Request is already ${current.status}`);
  }
  if (current.status === "cancelling") {
    return { status: "cancelling" }; // idempotent no-op
  }
  if (current.status === "queued") {
    const applied = await store.casTransition(requestId, tenantId, ["queued"], "cancelled");
    if (!applied) throw new ConflictError(`Request ${requestId} state changed concurrently`);
    return { status: "cancelled" };
  }
  const applied = await store.casTransition(requestId, tenantId, ["planning", "running"], "cancelling");
  if (!applied) throw new ConflictError(`Request ${requestId} state changed concurrently`);
  return { status: "cancelling" };
}

async function completeRequest(store: StatusStore, requestId: string, tenantId: string): Promise<void> {
  await store.casTransition(requestId, tenantId, ["running", "cancelling"], "succeeded");
  // false return is expected under the cancel/complete race and is silently dropped, not an error
}

async function finishCancellation(store: StatusStore, requestId: string, tenantId: string): Promise<void> {
  await store.casTransition(requestId, tenantId, ["cancelling"], "cancelled");
  // no-op if completeRequest already won the race
}
```
Renamed to `casTransition` (step 2's name — more accurate than step 1's `casUpdateStatus`, since it takes multiple `from` states, not a single prior value) and fixed a correctness gap present in both prior drafts: `cancelRequest` on the `queued`/non-`queued` paths now checks the `applied` boolean and throws `ConflictError` on a lost race instead of silently returning a possibly-stale status."}, {"step": 5, "title": "SSE resume handler (canonical)", "description": "```typescript
interface SseEvent {
  seq: number;
  event: "status" | "progress" | "step" | "resync";
  data: ExaixRequest;
}

interface EventBuffer {
  since(requestId: string, afterSeq: number): SseEvent[] | null; // null = buffer rolled off, caller must resync
}

async function streamRequestEvents(
  requestId: string,
  tenantId: string,
  lastEventId: string | null,
  buffer: EventBuffer,
  fetchCurrent: () => Promise<ExaixRequest>,
  write: (event: SseEvent) => void,
): Promise<void> {
  if (lastEventId !== null) {
    const afterSeq = Number.parseInt(lastEventId, 10);
    if (Number.isNaN(afterSeq)) throw new ValidationError("Invalid Last-Event-ID");
    const backlog = buffer.since(requestId, afterSeq);
    if (backlog === null) {
      const current = await fetchCurrent();
      write({ seq: afterSeq, event: "resync", data: current });
    } else {
      for (const evt of backlog) write(evt);
    }
  }
  // live subscription continues from here in the transport layer; stream ends after a terminal-state event
}
```
Adopted step 2's `Number.parseInt` + `NaN` guard (step 1 used a bare `Number()` cast with no validation, which would silently coerce a malformed `Last-Event-ID` header to `NaN` and mis-index the buffer) — malformed input is now a `400 ValidationError`, consistent with the boundary-validation rule from Security-First Development §1."}]}
